O alfabeto cirílico: por onde começar: The Cyrillic alphabet: where to start
PASSO 1: Uma cena que você já viveu (ou: STEP 1: A scene you have lived (or will live). Imagine it. You are in Russia. You come out of the metro and see a big sign, with strange letters that look like a secret code. The sign says: РЕСТОРАН You look at it and think: "That's impossible. It looks Chinese, it looks Greek, it looks... like nothing I know." You take a photo and give up. Now imagine the same scene one hour later. You look at the same sign and read it aloud: Restoran. It is the same word: restaurant. In Russian, restaurant is written ресторан. And the word has been right there in front of you from the start. You just could not read it. This lesson is about that hour. In sixty minutes of careful reading, you will be able to read any Russian sign. You will not understand every word yet, but you will read it. And that is the beginning of everything. STEP 2: The good news: you do not need to memorise 33 things. The Russian alphabet has 33 letters. When you see that number, your brain panics. "Thirty-three! Impossible!" But here is some good news: you do not need to memorise 33 letters. You need to memorise about 15. The other 18 you already know or recognise. How? Because Russian letters fall into four groups: • 1. Letters identical to English (5): A, K, M, O, T. • 2. Letters that look like English ones but have a different sound (7): В, Е, Н, Р, С, У, Х. • 3. New letters with sounds you already know (13): Б, Г, Д, Ё, З, И, Й, Л, П, Ф, Э, Ю, Я. • 4. Truly new letters with new sounds (8): Ж, Ц, Ч, Ш, Щ, Ъ, Ы, Ь. Total: 33 letters. But of the 4 groups, groups 1 and 2 are almost free. Group 3 you learn in an hour. Group 4 is the only one that takes effort. Let's go step by step. STEP 3: Before we start: why the alphabet is called Cyrillic. The Russian alphabet is called Cyrillic (кириллица) because it was created by Saint Cyril, a Greek monk, in the 9th century. He wanted to translate the Bible into the Slavic languages, and for that he needed an alphabet. Since he was Greek, he based the alphabet on Greek, with adaptations. What this means for you: many Russian letters look like Greek letters you have seen in maths, physics or elsewhere: Г (gamma) — looks like a reversed "g" Д (delta) — looks like a "d" with legs Л (lambda) — looks like an "l" with legs П (pi) — looks like a "p" with legs Ф (phi) — looks like an "f" with a circle If you have seen these Greek letters, you are already halfway there.
GRUPO 1 — As letras idênticas ao portugu: GROUP 1 — The letters identical to English. Five letters are the same as English in shape and sound. You already know them. You do not have to do anything. Notice: these five letters are identical to English. No trick. No exception. You already know them. Mental exercise: try to read these words using only these five letters: том → tom (volume) кот → koht (cat) мак → mahk (poppy) такт → tahkt (beat) ком → kohm (lump) You are already reading Russian. Without having studied anything. GROUP 2 — The "false friend" letters. Here is the first danger. There are seven letters that look like English letters but sound different. They are the "false friends": they look familiar, but they deceive you. I will give you a mnemonic table. Remember this: the golden rule of Group 2: if a letter looks Latin but is not, be suspicious. Russian borrowed the shape but changed the sound. Mental exercise: read these words with the false friends: вам → vahm (to you) нет → nyet (no) нос → nohs (nose) рука́ → roo-KAH (hand) сон → sohn (sleep, dream) ус → oos (moustache) хор → khohr (choir) You are already reading whole words in Russian.

GRUPO 3 — Letras novas com sons que você: GROUP 3 — New letters with sounds you already know. Here is the easy part. Thirteen letters are new in shape, but the sounds are ones you already know (or nearly). You only need to learn to link shape + sound. I will give you tricks for the most important ones: Б looks like "B", and it really is "B". Easy. Г looks like a reversed "G", and it is "G" as in go. Always hard. Д looks like a little house on legs, and it is "D". Ё is Е with two dots. Always stressed, sound "yo". З looks like a "3", and it is "Z" as in zebra. И looks like a reversed "N", and it is "EE". Й is И with an accent mark. A weak "y" sound. Л looks like an "L" with legs, and it is "L". П looks like a Greek "P" (pi), and it is "P". Ф looks like a Greek "F" (phi), and it is "F". Э looks like a mirrored "E", and it is an open "E", as in met. Ю is "Y" + "OO" together: sound "yoo". Я is "Y" + "A" together: sound "yah". Mental exercise: read these words: брат → braht (brother) го́род → GOH-raht (city) дом → dohm (house) ёлка → YOHL-kah (fir tree) зуб → zoop (tooth) игра́ → ee-GRAH (game) мой → moy (my) лампа → LAHM-pah (lamp) па́па → PAH-pah (dad) футбо́л → foot-BOHL (football) э́то → EH-tah (this is) юг → yook (south) я → yah (I) Notice: you have just read 13 Russian words. Without memorising any list. Without suffering.

GRUPO 4 — Letras realmente novas (e sons: GROUP 4 — Truly new letters (and new sounds). Here is the group that takes effort. There are eight letters with a new shape and a new sound. You really have to memorise them. I will explain each one calmly: Ж — like the «s» in «measure» Ж is the «zh» sound, as in «measure», «vision» or the «g» in «genre». It looks like a butterfly or an insect. жена́ → zhee-NAH (wife) журна́л → zhoor-NAHL (magazine) жизнь → zheezn (life) Ц — like the «ts» in «cats» Ц is the «ts» sound at the end of «cats» or «pizza». It looks like a «U» with a little tail. цена́ → tsee-NAH (price) центр → tsentr (center) коне́ц → kah-NYEHTS (end) Ч — like the «ch» in «chat» Ч is the «ch» sound of «chair». It looks like a «4». час → chahs (hour) чай → chy (tea) челове́к → chee-lah-VYEK (person) Ш — like the «sh» in «shop» Ш is the «sh» sound of «ship» and «shop». It looks like three vertical strokes joined at the bottom. шко́ла → SHKOH-lah (school) шапка → SHAHP-kah (hat) шум → shoom (noise) Щ — a longer, softer «sh-ch» Щ is a longer «sh» followed by a light «ch», as in «fresh cheese» said quickly. It looks like a «Ш» with a little tail. щи → shchee (cabbage soup) борщ → borshch (beet soup) това́рищ → tah-VAH-reeshch (comrade) Ъ — the hard sign (no sound) Ъ is a sign that has no sound of its own. It separates a consonant from a vowel, keeping the consonant hard. It appears in few words. объе́кт → ab-YEKT (object) объясни́ть → ab-yas-NEET (to explain) съесть → syest (to eat up) Ы — the throaty «ee» Ы is the hardest sound for English speakers. Say «ih» as in «bit», then pull your tongue back and down while keeping your lips relaxed and spread, not rounded. мы → mih (we) вы → vih (you) сын → sihn (son) ры́ба → RIH-bah (fish) Tip: say «ee», then pull your tongue back without moving your lips. The result is roughly «ы». Ь — the soft sign (no sound) Ь is a sign that has no sound of its own. It softens the consonant before it. That is, the consonant that comes before it is pronounced with a very light «y» after it. день → dyen' (day) ночь → noch' (night) мать → maht' (mother) слова́рь → slah-VAR' (dictionary) Tip: imagine you are saying the word and, at the end, you sketch a very light «y». That is it.

Tabela do alfabeto e escrita fonética: The alphabet table and phonetic spelling
A tabela completa do alfabeto russo. Aqu: The full table of the Russian alphabet. Here is the complete alphabet, in the correct order. Look at the columns: Note: the Cyrillic order is its own; it is inherited from the Greek alphabet. The big insight: the Russian alphabet is PHONETIC. Here is the most important thing in this lesson. Pay attention. In English, the same letter can have many sounds. Take the C: cat → «k» sound, city → «s» sound, church → «ch» sound, ocean → «sh» sound. Take «ough»: though, through, rough, cough, bough — five different sounds. This is a nightmare even for people learning English. But Russian is different. In Russian, each letter almost always has one fixed sound. Learn the letter, learn the sound. Full stop. There are two exceptions (we will see them in the next section), but they are predictable exceptions. Russian is much more phonetic than English. This is one of the reasons Russian is easier for an English speaker than it looks. You do not need to guess the pronunciation: you read it.

As duas regras de pronúncia que você pre: The two pronunciation rules you need to know now

The two pronunciation rules you need to know now. There are two pronunciation rules that show up from the very beginning. You need to learn them now. Rule 1: Unstressed «О» becomes «А» In Russian, the letter О sounds like «o» only when it is stressed (with the stress mark). When it is unstressed, it sounds like «a». Examples: This is why you will see spellings such as «mahsk-VAH» and «mah-lah-KOH» in books. That is the real pronunciation. Russians do not say «mohsk-VAH», they say «mahsk-VAH». What to do: when you learn a new word, learn it with the stress mark. Without the stress mark, you do not know whether the «o» is «o» or «a». Keep the word with its stress. Rule 2: Voiced consonants at the end become voiceless In Russian, if a word ends in a voiced consonant (Б, В, Г, Д, Ж, З), it is pronounced as the corresponding voiceless consonant (П, Ф, К, Т, Ш, С). Examples: This is why you will see spellings such as «drook» and «GOH-raht». That is the real pronunciation. Russians do not say «droog», they say «drook». What to do: when you learn a word, listen to the pronunciation. With time, your ear takes over.

Como reconhecer as letras na rua: How to recognise the letters on the street
Como reconhecer as letras na rua. Aqui e: How to recognise the letters on the street. Here is a mental exercise that changes everything. Imagine you are in Russia and you see a sign. You look at the sign and try to recognise the letters. Let's practise with real signs. Sign 1: РЕСТОРАН Р = R Е = YE С = S Т = T О = O Р = R А = A Н = N Result: RESTORAN = Restaurant. Sign 2: МЕТРО М = M Е = YE Т = T Р = R О = O Result: METRO = Metro. Sign 3: АПТЕКА А = A П = P Т = T Е = YE К = K А = A Result: APTEKA = Pharmacy. Sign 4: БАНК Б = B А = A Н = N К = K Result: BANK = Bank. Sign 5: ОТЕЛЬ О = O Т = T Е = YE Л = L Ь = soft sign Result: OTEL = Hotel. Sign 6: ТЕАТР Т = T Е = YE А = A Т = T Р = R Result: TEATR = Theatre. Notice: you have just read six Russian signs. Without memorising a complicated alphabet. Without suffering. That is what the Russian alphabet does. It is much friendlier than it looks.
Vogais duras e vogais brandas: a chave p: Hard vowels and soft vowels: the key to the consonants

Hard vowels and soft vowels: the key to the consonants. Here is a concept you need to understand from the start. It will appear in every lesson that follows. Russian vowels come in two families: HARD vowels (5): SOFT vowels (5): Notice: А ↔ Я (a ↔ ya) О ↔ Ё (o ↔ yo) У ↔ Ю (oo ↔ yoo) Э ↔ Е (e ↔ ye) Ы ↔ И (throaty ee ↔ ee) Each hard vowel has a matching soft vowel. This is fundamental because: when a consonant comes before a soft vowel, it is pronounced "softened" (palatalised). When it comes before a hard vowel, it is "hard". Examples: но (noh) → hard "n" нё (nyo) → softened "n" ну (noo) → hard "n" ню (nyoo) → softened "n" For now, you do not need to worry about this. But know that: the soft vowels (Я, Ё, Ю, Е, И) are the "secret" to understanding Russian consonants. Whenever you see one of these letters after a consonant, the consonant is "soft". We will see this in practice in the next section.
Consoantes surdas e sonoras; escrita cur: Voiceless and voiced consonants; cursive handwriting
As consoantes surdas e sonoras. Em russo: Voiceless and voiced consonants. In Russian, consonants fall into two groups, forming pairs: How it works: Voiceless consonants are pronounced without vibration of the vocal cords (like "p", "f", "k", "t", "s", "sh"). Voiced consonants are pronounced with vibration of the vocal cords (like "b", "v", "g", "d", "z", "zh"). The rule: when a voiced consonant is at the end of a word, it is pronounced as the matching voiceless one. Examples: This is why "друг" sounds like "drook". The letter Г at the end of the word becomes К. How to write in Russian cursive. An important detail: Russians write in cursive very often. You will see handwritten texts with letters different from the printed ones. Here is a small table of the main differences: For now, focus on the printed letters. When you come across handwritten Russian texts, you will learn cursive little by little.
